walk.title: Solve it: a prompt that turns any order into clean JSON
walk.sample: 10 test messages in English, Pidgin and Yoruba · e.g. "abeg bring 3 bag onion come Bodija tomorrow morning"

steps.say: Customers still type orders in English, Pidgin and Yoruba. We'll write a prompt that turns them into clean JSON, and prove it with a test, not a hope.
show: Goal: 10 out of 10 on the test set

steps.say: Build the exam before the student. Ten messages, normal and tricky, each with the right answer written down first.
show: #10 a price question, not an order

steps.say: Version one is the obvious one-line prompt. It looks fine on message one, but on the full set only four answers are usable.
show: Extract the order from this customer message as JSON.

steps.say: Look at why. Markdown fences break the parser, an address and quantity were invented, and ugwu became pepper.
Version two adds a role, the SKU catalogue, only JSON, null when something isn't stated, and ISO dates from today's date.
Two still fail, because customers say rodo and the red one, and the catalogue only knew scotch bonnet.
show: Message 9: guessed rodo for "the red one"

steps.say: Version three teaches the model our world: the local names customers really use, and one worked example in Pidgin.
show: PEP-ROF-L rodo / ata rodo / scotch bonnet

steps.say: It also gets a needs confirmation flag. Anything uncertain, or not an order at all, is marked for a human to check.
Compare the three versions side by side. Each one fixed the failures the last one revealed, and you can see it in the score.
Check the hard ones. Message ten is a price question, so items is empty and it's flagged for Tolu.
Notice what the AI is not allowed to do: no prices and no totals. The sheet from Module 0.4 does the maths with formulas.
And a rules step checks every answer: does it parse, are the SKUs real, is every quantity above zero? Anything that fails goes to Tolu, not the sheet.

walk.end: Tested on ten messages, scored, and improved until it passed: that's a prompt you can put inside an automation.
